outcome_summary: All four emptied worktrees restored. Zero mass deletions remain. Object database verified intact. No commit was created from the damaged state at any point.

process_audit.method: Win32_Process enumeration via CIM; command lines searched for opencode, worktree, git clean, Remove-Item, rmdir, rd /s, rmtree, os.remove, unlink, git reset, git checkout, git restore, cleanup, prune, Temp, worktrees

process_audit.conclusion: Nothing was actively deleting at audit time. The damage was already done and is historical.

reasoning: All four emptied worktrees live under C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\, which is the scratch root the opencode.exe agents themselves use.
In each worktree the ONLY surviving file was the .git pointer file (92-101 bytes) -- every tracked file was removed while the gitdir pointer was left behind.
Three separate opencode.exe sessions are running, so multiple agents could have operated in that tree.

That signature is consistent with a session/scratch cleanup that removed the CONTENTS of registered worktree directories it did not own, rather than with git itself: `git reset --hard` or `git checkout .` would RESTORE files, not empty the tree, and `git clean` would not remove tracked files.
No `git reset` can explain this, so the earlier reflog hint is explicitly NOT treated as the cause.
root_cause.not_established: The exact command and session cannot be attributed from process state alone after the fact. PowerShell history and agent logs were not available within this batch.
root_cause.hardening_recommendation: Move all git worktrees out of the agent scratch root. A registered worktree inside a temp directory that an agent lifecycle manages is the structural hazard, independent of which agent misbehaved.

forensic_evidence.deliberately_outside_temp: Written to G: because Temp\opencode is itself the suspect path.

untracked_forensic.finding: No untracked evidence existed to preserve. The sole survivor in each worktree was the untracked .git pointer file, recorded in the JSON evidence.

forensic_evidence.index_decision: Because staged == 0, RESTORE_SOURCE = HEAD and the index was never touched. `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- .` was used. No `git reset --hard` at any point.

class_2_git_lfs.evidence: Worktree bytes equal HEAD blob bytes exactly (tile_0_0.xodr: 2288486 == 2288486; scene.glb likewise). The apparent '42,349 deletions / 3 insertions' is the LFS clean filter converting real content to a 3-line pointer during diff, not missing data.
class_2_git_lfs.verification: Worktree file read directly from disk: 42,349 lines of real OpenDRIVE XML with correct header; git cat-file -s HEAD:<path> == worktree size.
class_2_git_lfs.note: This also explains the 'Encountered 18 files that should have been pointers' message emitted during restore.

residual_classification.total_recovered_lines: 12.6M lines per worktree restored from the object database; no line was lost.
prevention_recommended: Relocate git worktrees out of C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\. The structural fix is that a registered worktree must not live inside an agent-managed scratch root.
Add a guard that refuses any recursive delete whose target contains a .git entry or appears in `git worktree list`.
Require cleanup jobs to log canonical target, resolved path, file count and planned operation.
Never run `git add -A` automatically after a bulk filesystem cleanup.

mass_deletion_commit_check.method: All four worktrees were inspected in the damaged state; restore was performed from HEAD without staging, so no commit could encode the deletion. No commit, push, branch creation or history rewrite occurred at any point in this recovery.
